strengths.text: Persistent bottom bar keeps the betting loop (Sports · Betslip · My bets · Account) one tap away from anywhere.
Betslip is a self-contained sheet — Betslip↔My bets pill, an “accept odds change” toggle, and clear stake/odds/payout.
Sport + market selections persist in the URL — browser back/refresh keep the user’s place.
Casino & Virtuals keep the product header (Sports/Live/Casino/Virtuals) — consistent within those products.

frictions.text: Bottom bar represents only Sports of the four products — Home/Live/Casino/Virtuals aren’t in the bar.
No active state on Home/Casino/Virtuals; on Live the bar highlights “Sports” — absent/conflicting “you are here”.
Entering Sports/Live replaces the product switcher with the sports sub-nav — you can’t reach Casino/Virtuals from within Sports without the Menu.
Three overlapping nav surfaces (header + bottom bar + full-screen Menu) duplicate the same destinations.
My Bets is reachable three ways (bottom-nav bets page, betslip pill, Account drawer) with different presentations.
Help / Support has no top-level entry — it lives only inside the Account drawer.
The bottom bar changes between logged-out and logged-in (Join Now ↔ My bets).
No labelled “Home” anywhere — the homepage is reachable only via the logo and an unlabelled sub-nav icon; nothing in the header or bottom bar says Home.

No single, obvious “Home”: the logo returns to the homepage while the bottom-nav “Sports” opens the events list — two different pages. A dedicated Home in the bottom bar, in the thumb zone, would give one clear way back.
The in-content home shortcut is inconsistent — the sub-nav home icon appears on Sports/Casino/Virtuals but is replaced by “Upcoming” on Live, and it’s an icon-only ~40px tap target.

strengths.text: Live events featured above the fold, easily visible on top navigation.
Can find live events on home page, with indication of how many more are available.
Can easily sort and filter; applied filters clearly visible and easy to clear.
Shows the number of live events under each category.

frictions.text: Live events is the last option and easily missed. We also don’t show this whole column for other sports besides football; when the user switches to another sport, football is still prioritised on the homepage’s live section.
Live event count mismatches within the same session (Home “Live 7” pill vs. “Live 15” section header).
Type chips (Outrights/Upcoming/Live) and competition chips (UEFA CL/EL) share one scrollable row with no visual grouping — unclear where one category ends and the next begins.
Individual live rows mix sports (football, tennis) with no sport icon, only a text label — recall over recognition.
Floating “Back to top” pill overlaps live list content at the bottom of the scroll.
User expects to see the 15 more live games, but the default list comes short since other games sit under other categories — misleading.
It’s not clear how to search for a specific game from this list; the search icon up top is easy to miss, and search results navigate the user away from the page.
Nothing distinguishes “actively updating” from “frozen” — just silent time jumps.
No visible default sort logic on the default live page.
Some events don’t show market selections on the match card.
The 1UP & 2UP fixed section reduces the view area — the user ends up seeing only two match cards per view.

strengths.text: Markets have explainers that show on demand.
User can search for a market without exiting the page.

frictions.text: Tooltip text is cut off and auto-closes on scroll.
Search returns different results depending on which tab you’re in, with no indication of why or which tab is being searched — a hidden boundary.
Search empty state has no way to broaden the search (e.g. “search all markets”) — a dead end.
Exiting search navigates the user back to the “All” tab even when a different tab was active.
Navigating back to the live events list doesn’t update the list right away.

strengths.text: Half-time indicators are present.
Clear ‘why’ and next action for the user.

frictions.text: Live indicator reverts to the scheduled kickoff time instead of a HT badge while the event is still ongoing — miscommunication between the 3rd-party stats game time and betPawa.
Markets disappear and reappear with no genuine loading state (skeleton) to show whether the page loaded.
At times the live page shows the second half has started but the details page doesn’t update for ~20 seconds.

strengths.text: Odds-change direction is shown clearly.
“Accept odds change” toggle correctly gates behaviour.
Clear indication of locked and unavailable selections.

frictions.text: No actual time & score for live events — hard to tell if the score changed since your last selection.
“Accept odds change” is auto-toggled off when odds change.
The “Odds changed” banner doesn’t get dismissed.
“Locked” and “Unavailable” are two different badges with no explanation of what distinguishes them (temporarily suspended vs. permanently gone?).
Error banner says “Click ‘Place bet without N/A’” but the actual button reads “PLACE BET WITHOUT LOCKED”.
Selection order re-shuffles between states (a team moves bottom → top → bottom) with no user action.

strengths.text: Live legs show the live badge, half and time.

frictions.text: Distinct visuals for live stats create more inconsistency.
There are cases where the ‘minimize stats’ action within the widget doesn’t show up.
Opening the inline stats panel pushes the remaining legs a full scroll below, and the viewpoint is off — the maximize/minimize interaction is frustrating.
Two different disclaimer strings cover the same thing.
Clicking on events navigates the user back to Upcoming.
Sometimes we show full stats, sometimes we don’t.
Inconsistent opening behaviour of live stats (expand vs. bottom-sheet).

strengths.text: Categorized tabs provide structured navigation across primary wagering categories.
Detailed headers and item counts streamline content consumption without cognitive overload.
Granular status labels clearly communicate real-time progress for individual selections inside multi-leg wagers.
Active tab highlighting offers strong feedback vs. competitors (contrasting badge colours would optimise it further).
A functional return-to-top control enables rapid upward navigation without obscuring card elements.
Essential wagering details remain clearly grouped within the primary visual focus area.
The share trigger occupies a high-visibility position that reinforces social features.
Bet cards display full context: sport type, tournament name, and league details.

frictions.text: Header tabs stay fixed but trigger navigation to unrelated screens outside the My Bets section — unexpected flows and navigational confusion.
Secondary navigation tabs don’t stay pinned during vertical scrolling, forcing users to scroll back up to switch views.
Bet ID values are static text with no copy functionality — reduced utility for support or reference.
Date attributes are correct, but a more structured visual layout (à la BetKing) would improve hierarchy and legibility.
Grey informational boxes occupy disproportionate screen space — an opportunity for more compact UI.
Bet cards lack selection details despite available space — preview components or expandable accordions would add instant clarity.
The Re-use button sits above match listings, creating ambiguity about targeted selections — move it below the specific games.
No explicit tap-to-copy for unique wagering identifiers.
Status badges show game state but cards lack rich live visualisations, field movement, and clear event identifiers.
Users can’t tap through to primary event pages from within bet cards — breaks expected exploration paths.
Leg selection lists blend into general bet info — distinct container boundaries would aid visual parsing.

strengths.text: The Cashout section sits in a logical position within the screen hierarchy.
The action happens directly on the page with fast response times.
The status label is placed in a correct and visually prominent location.

frictions.text: Cashout information is completely absent despite the corresponding badge in the UI.
Show the Cashout amount upfront (like competitors); wide spacing between header and Request button creates uncertainty about the outcome.
Advanced Cashout functionality available on competitor platforms is entirely missing.
The status label after Cashout lacks clarity, and the header doesn’t use past tense to signal completion.
Feedback after Cashout relies solely on the top label — no supporting toast or confirmation popup.

strengths.text: Differentiation looks well executed across the layout.
The internal card design is strong and distinguishes itself from a regular win (needs clearer explanations and UI refinement).
The Share button has an impressive visual design that draws appropriate attention.

frictions.text: This banner permanently occupies too much space while limiting sorting — a dedicated filter button with deep customisation would be better.
All negative aspects from the Open Bets card persist here; Settled cards should be more clearly distinct from Open bets.
Essential sharing functionality is completely absent directly on the card.
The reason for celebrating this win with confetti and a trophy is unclear, and the iconography looks cluttered/unrecognisable without zooming in.
A dropdown pattern for Open bet details plus full-page navigation for Settled bets would maximise usability.
The card doesn’t clearly communicate whether a game is won or lost — requires deep analysis vs. immediate visual cues used by competitors.
Sharing is heavily constrained and falls behind competitors — needs significant expansion and customisation.
Play up the block titles and add illustrations to visually help users.
Adding screenshots or videos would make it more convenient for the user.
A search would make it easier for users to find the information they need.
Play up the block titles and add illustrations to visually help users.
A search would make it easier for users to find the information they need.
Add navigation within this page — by sport types and so on.
Too many filter tabs at the top — the user scrolls a long horizontal row just to find the category they want.
Games have no Demo option or info/description button — no way to preview a game or learn how it works before committing real money.
The “Home” tab inside Casino should be renamed to “Recommended”, so users don’t think tapping it leaves Casino for the site homepage.
A large number of games are hidden behind scrolling — the user might not notice them.
The confirmation modal for removing from favourites is unnecessary — the action is minor and instantly reversible.
The sorting may confuse users — there’s “Popular” in sorting and also one at the top.
With many recent searches, we stop suggesting games — we could limit the number or hide the older ones.
Users may be more used to seeing the navigation at the top.
Show the number of players / likes / total plays to build interest.
When the user closes a casino game the app closes immediately, with no attempt to retain them (e.g. suggesting other games).
Banners between game category blocks look low quality — like static screenshots with a fake baked-in CTA button; the whole banner is the click target, making the button misleading.
There’s no block with recent wins in casino games.
There’s no action to delete all recent searches at once.
The illustrations don’t catch the eye.
Multiple entries essentially lead to the same Virtuals game and take up a lot of space.
There aren’t many objects here — the layout could show everything to the user at once.
Not much interactivity — no promotions, banners, etc. to engage the user.
Show some big recent wins to draw the user in.
A timer on the virtual thumbnail could show when the next match starts.
Show the league selection at the top.
It’s unclear where the Next button leads.
Show more clearly that the match is live — maybe with an animation or illustration.
The active betslip isn’t very noticeable.
Consider a dedicated betslip on the Virtuals page to remove noise and focus the user on the action.

strengths.text: Clear top-to-bottom hierarchy — balance & nav, then promos, then combos, then match lists.
Balance and a one-tap Deposit ‘+’ sit top-right on landing — funding is always one tap away.
The persistent ‘up to 1250% Win Bonus’ footer nudges accumulator building without blocking content.
Sticky bottom nav keeps Sports / Betslip / My bets / Account one tap away throughout the scroll.
A consistent green marks every actionable odd and CTA — a clear ‘tap here’ visual language.
Home leads with 'Popular Match Combos' — pre-built multi-selection bets accelerate the core action right on the homepage.

frictions.text: Three promo cards plus the bonus banner push real match lists well below the fold.
Casino Cashback is the first promo card on a sports home — casino cross-sell ahead of sport.
The three promo cards are visually near-identical (‘Read More’), so no single offer stands out.
Every visit starts by scrolling past promos.

strengths.text: One tap adds a full pre-built combo and the win-bonus updates instantly — very low friction.
Combos surface pre-built multi-leg bets right on the homepage — accelerates the core action.
Each combo lists its legs (Double Chance, Over 1.5, Multigoals) so bettors see exactly what they’re backing.
Combined odds are shown on every combo card — the payout is clear before adding to the slip.

frictions.text: The betslip is only a thin summary bar — no obvious way to review or edit the legs.
The win-bonus grows as legs stack, but the multiplier mechanic isn't explained inline — low trust.
Combos are fixed bundles — there’s no way to drop or swap a leg before adding it.
The betslip bar shows odds and bonus but not the number of selections — unclear what’s in the slip.

strengths.text: Each promo has a dedicated, well-explained page with a single clear CTA.
Each promo page leads with one bold value prop and a single BET NOW CTA — no decision overload.
Each promo page includes a plain-language ‘What makes it different / How it works’ breakdown.
A single BET NOW / PLAY NOW CTA per page keeps the next step obvious.

frictions.text: Promo pages are separate destinations with no ‘back to bet’ shortcut — users can lose their place.
Casino cashback is promoted on the homepage home — cross-sell competes with sports intent.
Promo pages are long marketing scrolls — the actual terms and limits sit well below the fold.
Three overlapping bonuses (Win Bonus, Early Wins, Cashback) with no comparison — unclear which applies when.

flows.flow: Sports Discovery · Browse & filter a sport

strengths.text: Layered filters — Leagues + Markets + Date — with live event counts give precise control.
Filter overlays show a live event count per league, so users pick populated markets.
Reset / Apply in the filter overlays gives a clear, reversible commit — no accidental filtering.
Popular Leagues are surfaced first with live counts — a fast path to the biggest markets.
'Show 1UP & 2UP' toggle and hot-odds markers appear across every list — boosted markets are easy to spot.

frictions.text: Filters open as separate overlays; there's no single view of all active filters at once.
Applied filters aren't summarised on the results list — easy to forget what's active.
The market filter is a long radio list with no search — finding a specific market is slow.
Date sits in a separate dropdown from the day tabs — two ways to pick a day is confusing.

strengths.text: Rich in-play: a live match visualiser with continuously updating stats and markets.
Live minute and score sit on every in-play row — instant context before opening a match.
In-play odds and markets update live without a manual refresh — the slip stays current.
Event sub-tabs (Match · Statistics · Head-to-head · Standings) keep all context in one place.

frictions.text: Many live markets show as locked with no ETA — dead affordances mid-match.
The in-play visualiser dominates the first screen, pushing the actual markets down.
The ‘Show 1UP & 2UP’ toggle tops the live list with no hint of what 1UP / 2UP actually does.
No way to filter out finished or one-market live events — the list carries dead rows.

strengths.text: Built-in statistics (H2H, form, win probability) support the bet decision in-context.
Markets are grouped into scannable tabs (All/Popular/Goals/Halves) with counts.
Win-probability bar + previous meetings give quick form context before betting.
Market groups carry counts (Popular 18 · Goals 40 · Halves) so bettors gauge depth at a glance.

frictions.text: Statistics fill the whole first screen; the actual markets sit far below the fold.
Market-group tabs scroll horizontally and can hide options off-screen.
Every market row has an unlabeled info (i) icon — its purpose isn’t clear.
Stats sections expand / collapse via small carets — the extra data is easy to miss.
